slides.purpose: State the answer and the ask up front
slides.headline: Promotions are destroying value: reject the 20% budget increase and refocus 2026 on Fresh and Beverages
slides.reason_to_exist: Board members need the answer and the decision in one page

slides.purpose: Show the escalation of promotional intensity
slides.headline: Promotions rose from 29% to 38% of sales in FY2025, at an average depth up from 18% to 24%
slides.reason_to_exist: Establishes that the business already promotes heavily, before asking for more

slides.headline: Promoted volume grew 14% but full-price volume fell 6%, so total volume grew only 2.1%
slides.reason_to_exist: Directly tests marketing's claim that promotions drove volume growth

slides.purpose: Explain why promotions do not add volume
slides.headline: 71% of promoted volume goes to customers who also buy at full price, and their sales drop 22% in the two weeks after a promotion ends
slides.reason_to_exist: Gives the causal mechanism (subsidy and forward buying) behind the flat volume
slides.why_not_merge: S3 shows the outcome at total level; S4 shows the customer-level mechanism from a different data set (loyalty card) — merging would overload one slide

slides.headline: Gross margin fell 2.3 pp, from 27.4% to 25.1%, as promotional depth rose 6 pp
slides.reason_to_exist: The CFO needs the margin impact, not just volume
slides.why_not_merge: Volume (S3/S4) and margin are two distinct consequences; margin carries its own caveat on causality
slides.caveat: Correlation, not a margin bridge: non-promotional drivers (H6) not excluded

slides.purpose: Show where promotion creates and destroys value
slides.headline: Per hundred euros of promotion, Household (−3.4 EUR) and Snacks (−2.1 EUR) lose margin while Fresh (+1.6 EUR) and Beverages (+0.8 EUR) gain
slides.reason_to_exist: Category economics determine where to cut and where to keep promotion

slides.purpose: Confront the marketing proposal with the evidence
slides.decision_role: evaluates the option on the table
slides.headline: Marketing's plan would raise the promotion budget 20% and deepen discounts in Household, the category with the worst return
slides.reason_to_exist: The board is asked to approve this proposal; it must see it tested explicitly
slides.why_not_merge: S6 is the neutral category diagnosis; S7 applies it to the specific proposal under decision

slides.purpose: Set out the 2026 plan and next steps
slides.headline: 2026 plan: hold the budget, cut depth in Household and Snacks, target Fresh and Beverages, and confirm with a margin bridge and tests
slides.reason_to_exist: Converts the diagnosis into the decision the board must take
